Kuvitus: sairaalan PET-TT-kuvaushuone. K: Illustration: a hospital PET-CT scanning room. In the middle is a large white scanner with a round opening. A patient lies under a blanket on a scanning table that slides into the opening. On the left wall is a window to the control room, where a screen shows a dark cross-sectional image with one bright orange spot.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: röntgenkuva: Schematic, not to scale: X-ray imaging. At the top is a glass X-ray tube: on the left a glowing cathode, from which electrons are accelerated to the right towards the anode. X-ray photons leave the anode downwards as a fan of wavy lines. In their path is a cross-section of a forearm: soft tissue with two bones inside it. Photons that hit the bones are stopped, and the others continue through the tissue to the detector below. A lighter shadow appears on the detector where the bones are, because less radiation reaches it there.
Schematic, not to scale: PET imaging. On the left is a cross-section of the patient in the middle of a detector ring. Inside the body a fluorine-18 nucleus emits a positron, which travels a short distance and meets an electron. Two photons leave the meeting point in opposite directions and hit two detectors of the ring, which are coloured orange. A dashed line segment is drawn between the detectors, and the annihilation must have happened on it. On the right is an enlargement: a positron and an electron meet, and two photons of 511 kiloelectronvolts are produced, leaving at an angle of 180 degrees to each other.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: sädehoito v: Schematic, not to scale: radiotherapy from five directions. In the middle of a cross-section of the patient is a tumour. Five radiation beams come from outside the body from different directions, and each passes through the tumour and through the body. The beams intersect only at the tumour, so the tumour receives the dose of five beams, 5 times 0.40 gray, that is, 2.0 gray. Healthy tissue along a beam receives the dose of only one beam, about 0.40 gray.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: paperikonee: Schematic, not to scale: the thickness gauge of a paper machine. A horizontal paper web runs from left to right between two pairs of rollers. Below the web is a beta radiation source, from which electrons travel upwards as blue dots through the paper. Some are stopped in the paper, and some reach the detector above the web. A wire from the detector carries the reading to a controller, which adjusts the pressure of the rollers: the thicker the paper, the less radiation gets through.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: läpi päässeen rön: Graph to scale: the share of X-radiation that gets through, I per I zero, as a function of the thickness d of the layer, with the thickness from zero to 8 centimetres and the photon energy about 60 kiloelectronvolts. In soft tissue the share halves after every 3.4 centimetres, in bone already after 1.1 centimetres: at 1.1 centimetres half gets through bone and at 2.2 centimetres a quarter, while half gets through soft tissue at 3.4 centimetres. The curve for bone therefore falls much more steeply.
